evidence: Authority, tool ID/version, schema digest, role, route, mutation, confirmation, active registration generation, and provenance metadata are explicit without merging executors; the local provider key is not treated as server authority.

title: Implement server-side capability lease lifecycle
evidence: Graph OS owns authorization, lease/call/replay state and receipts; issue/renew/revoke/expiry is bound to server-verified login session, actor/principal, tenant, session, origin, document, route, active generation, policy, tool, nonce, attended opt-in, and trace state; no service credential is sent to or treated as user delegation by the browser.

title: Implement authenticated browser bridge and local dispatcher
evidence: Only named local tools execute under a Graph OS-verified lease and active registration generation with attended opt-in; unsupported WebMCP remains a no-op and lifecycle changes retire registrations.

title: Route calls through one Graph OS BrowserControlService with at-most-once fences
evidence: REST, MCP, workflow, and WebMCP use one Graph OS BrowserControlService and authorization/control operation; a durable pre-dispatch fence prevents duplicate browser side effects, and raw query/request surfaces are rejected.

title: Implement cross-boundary cancellation, expiry, replay, and disconnect handling
evidence: All terminal conditions are idempotent; cancellation reports none, browser_reported_committed, or unknown without claiming rollback or unconditional late-effect rejection, and unknown outcomes are reconciled.

title: Emit governed provenance and observability receipt
evidence: Graph OS durably audits before dispatch and every outcome carries bounded verified session/actor/tenant/principal/document/route/generation, lease, policy, nonce/fence, timing, result/error, cancellation effect, truthful Langfuse status, and RunTrace evidence or explicit telemetry-unavailable state.

evidence: Static checks prove route coverage, no duplicate authorities, active-generation metadata, asset and image policy, legal/contact completeness, consent singularity, trust-prerequisite gating, and secret boundaries.
